The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. facts.text: “Man, Arturo. I don't even know where we stand half the time. We're teammates, sure, and we've got that bond from grinding through the minors together, but lately it feels like he's got one foot in the big leagues and one foot back here in Oakland, and I'm just... here. He doesn't call as much, and when we do talk, it's all about pitch counts and bullpen sessions, not the real stuff. I still got love for him, but I've stopped expecting him to show up like he used to, you know? It's not anger — it's just this quiet acceptance that we're on different paths now, and that's okay, even if it stings a little.” — Marco Fabregas, Catcher, Las Vegas Aviators (AAA), Laurel (own page, the night page, C112)

“The little thing is the way the coffee shop guy—Marcus, I think?—remembered my order without me saying it. It’s dumb, but it felt like being seen. I don’t get that a lot, not really, not in a city that big. It made me want to be that kind of person, the one who notices. Or maybe it just made me feel less invisible, and that’s enough.” — Eleanor Fong, student, Chinatown (own page, the morning page, C112)
